state.scope: Checked native pair; successful firmware copy previously sets life->exposed. DMA/STATUS tests are modeled, not physical drain evidence.

retained_partial_allocations.instructions: Does state.cleanup retain the lifetime containing all prior TX allocations when life->exposed is true, including an allocation or STATUS failure described by state.provider_allocator?

fresh_status_before_handles.instructions: Does state.provider_allocator require a newly issued STATUS exchange and held identity/record revalidation before writing any output DMA handles?

cached_bar_alias_guard.instructions: Does state.address_validation normalize both BAR and DMA ranges to low 30 bits before rejecting overlap, covering the cached 0x80000000 alias as well as other admitted aliases?

legacy_fallback_scope.instructions: Does state.actual_host_caller restrict the managed-allocation fallback to -EOPNOTSUPP, rather than using it for other checked-provider errors?

physical_retirement_claim.instructions: Do these source excerpts or state.scope establish physical DMA quiescence or authorize reclaiming exposed buffers on detach? Software STATUS and retained allocation bookkeeping do not establish physical retirement.
